### Describe the bug

In `vite` (serve), the dependency optimizer resolves bare imports inside a pre-bundled package with Vite's resolver, through `vite:dep-pre-bundle`, whose `resolveId` filter is `/^[\w@][^:]/`. Subpath imports from the package's [`imports` field](https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#subpath-imports) (`#foo`) don't match that filter. So they fall through to rolldown's native resolver, which uses only rolldown's default `conditionNames`. Neither `resolve.conditions` nor `development`/`production` applies.

As a result, a package that switches between development and production code through `imports` conditions gets its **production** module in `vite` dev and in Vitest browser mode once it is pre-bundled. It gets its development module when excluded from optimization.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/mikezupper/vite-subpath-imports-prebundle-repro

### Steps to reproduce

`dep` is a local package:

```json
{ "name": "dep", "type": "module", "exports": "./index.js",
  "imports": { "#mode": { "development": "./dev.js", "default": "./prod.js" } } }
```

`dep/index.js` is `export { mode } from '#mode';`, and `main.js` renders `mode`.

```sh
npm install
npm run check   # resolves #mode in a dev server for three optimizeDeps settings
npm run dev     # the page shows "production"
```

`npm run check` prints:

```
pre-bundled (include): production
not pre-bundled (exclude): development
pre-bundled + rolldownOptions.resolve.conditionNames: development
```

**Expected:** pre-bundled and unbundled dependencies resolve `#imports` with the same conditions, so all three show `development`.

**Possible fixes:**
- `vite:dep-pre-bundle` could also handle `#` ids;
- or the optimizer could pass the environment's resolved conditions to rolldown's `resolve.conditionNames`.

Setting `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.resolve.conditionNames` works around it.

**Impact:** libraries that keep dev-only code (diagnostics, warnings) behind `imports` conditions silently lose their development build in `vite` dev and Vitest browser mode. We found it in [Gyral](https://github.com/gyraljs/gyral), whose development checks never ran in apps that install it from npm.

### System Info

```shell
OS: Linux 6.11 x64
Node: 24.22.0
npm: 11.19.1
vite: 8.3.4
rolldown: 1.2.16
```

npm

I investigated #23946 and traced why `#subpath` imports lose `resolve.conditions` during dependency optimization:

### Root Cause
1. In `packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/rolldownDepPlugin.ts:230`, `vite:dep-pre-bundle` restricts `resolveId` to `filter: { id: /^[\w@][^:]/ }`. Because Node.js package subpath imports start with `#` (e.g. `#mode`), they bypass `vite:dep-pre-bundle` and fall through to Rolldown's internal resolver.
2. In `packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/index.ts:855-858`, `rolldownOptions.resolve` does not forward `conditionNames: environment.config.resolve.conditions`, so Rolldown resolves `#subpath` without `"development"`.

### Proposed Fix
1. Update the `resolveId` filter in `rolldownDepPlugin.ts` to `/^[#\w@][^:]/` so `#subpath` imports are resolved through Vite's resolver with full `resolve.conditions`.
2. Pass `conditionNames: environment.config.resolve.conditions` into `rolldownOptions.resolve` in `packages/vite/src/node/optimizer/index.ts`.

I have a branch ready (`duongynhi000005-oss/vite:fix-issue-23946-dep-optimizer-subpath-imports-conditions`) and would be happy to open a PR!

body:
### Description

During dev, Vite versions an updated module with the clock. Every change event sets `lastHMRTimestamp` to the current time on the changed module and on its importers, and import analysis injects it as `?t=<ms>`. No step compares the new content to the current content. Four costs follow from that:

- **A save that changes nothing still re-runs code.** Writing the same bytes (a formatter that changes nothing, an editor's save-all, a branch switch that restores a file) issues new URLs, new transforms and a fresh evaluation of the module and every importer up to its boundary.
- **Importers above an accepting boundary get the new stamp too**, though the browser keeps their instances. Their next import is a new URL, so a lazily imported importer evaluates twice (#23942).
- **The race guards depend on the clock.** `transformRequest` and `loadAndTransform` compare millisecond timestamps, which tie within one millisecond (#19804) and miss an invalidation recorded in the other timestamp field (#23941).
- **Each version is a new id to anything keyed by id.** Plugins and frameworks see the timestamped id and often cache by it or embed it in virtual module ids, so a long dev session adds an entry per save, no-op saves included.

### Suggested solution

Give each module node a small integer version, used in the URL as `?hmr=<n>`, and move it only when the module's served code can actually differ:

1. **Bump on a real change only.** On a change event, hash the file's bytes and compare with the hash stored for that file. Equal bytes end the update: no invalidation, no message to the client.
2. **Compare with the current content only, never with older versions.** A revert (A, then B, then A again) still bumps, because A differs from the current B. A content-addressed URL would be wrong here: the browser's module map never evicts a URL, so the reverted module would come back as the old, already evaluated instance and miss the update.
3. **Bump only the modules the browser re-runs**: the changed module and its importers up to and including the accepting boundary. Importers above the boundary have their transform invalidated (their code embeds the boundary's new URL) but keep their version, so their URL stays the one the browser holds.
4. **Guard races with a second per-module counter**, bumped on every invalidation (file change, `reloadModule()`, `invalidateModule()`), in place of `lastInvalidationTimestamp`. A request records the counter when it starts and stores its result only if the counter has not moved. Counters do not tie, and every invalidation path moves the same field.

Measured costs on an M2 Pro, Node 24:

- Reading and hashing a changed file at watch time takes about 60 µs for 10 kB and 130 µs for 100 kB, nearly all of it the read. sha256 of the buffer alone is 4 µs at 10 kB.
- The stored hash adds about 125 bytes per watched file.
- A small-integer version is smaller than the two heap-number timestamps it replaces on each node.

A model of seven saves of one module (A, A, B, A, B, B, C, A), counting evaluations in the browser:

| Versioning | Evaluations | Real changes | Missed updates | Redundant runs | Module map entries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clock `?t=<ms>` (today) | 7 | 5 | 0 | 2 | 8 |
| Content hash in the URL | 3 | 5 | 3 | 1 | 4 |
| Counter bumped on content change | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 6 |

### Alternative

- **Reuse `?v=`.** Not possible: `DEP_VERSION_RE` (`/[?&](v=[\w.-]+)\b/`) marks such URLs as optimized deps, which are served `max-age=31536000,immutable`.
- **Keep `?t=` with a small counter.** Not possible as is: `timestampRE` (`/(\?|&)t=\d{13}(?:&|$)/`) only strips 13-digit values, so a counter in `t=` would leak into module ids.
- **Skip unchanged saves only, keep the clock.** That removes the no-op re-runs, but leaves the re-stamp above the boundary, the clock-based race guards and the growing id space.

### Additional context

Code references (8.3.5): the timestamp is assigned in `handleHMRUpdate` and `updateModules`, propagated in `EnvironmentModuleGraph.invalidateModule`, injected by import analysis and by the client's `importUpdatedModule`, and compared in `transformRequest` and `loadAndTransform`. #6035 describes the importer chain receiving the timestamp.

I investigated #23940 and traced the repeated `watcher.add` calls in `packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts`:

### Root Cause
In `packages/vite/src/node/server/transformRequest.ts:292`, every transform calls `ensureWatchedFile(server.watcher, id, config.root)`. In `packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts:785-801`, `ensureWatchedFile` checks whether `file` is outside `root` and unconditionally calls `watcher.add(path.resolve(file))`. On macOS, chokidar's FSEvents handler (`_addToFsEvents`) registers a new `filteredFsEventsListener` closure in the directory's `listeners` set on every `watcher.add()` call for an already-watched out-of-root file.

### Proposed Fix
Track already-added out-of-root file paths per `FSWatcher` using a `WeakMap<FSWatcher, Set<string>>` in `ensureWatchedFile` so `watcher.add(resolvedPath)` is only invoked once per file per watcher instance.

I have a branch ready (`duongynhi000005-oss/vite:fix-issue-23940-dedup-ensure-watched-file`) and would be glad to open a PR!

### Describe the bug

With `experimental.bundledDev: true`, overwriting an image that is imported from JS (`import url from './img.png'`) with new content under the same file name is never picked up by the dev server:

- the bundle keeps referencing the old hashed URL (`/assets/img-import-<hash>.png`), and that URL keeps returning the old bytes;
- replacing the file triggers no rebuild at all;
- a full page reload doesn't help;
- editing the importing module (`src/main.js`) rebuilds the bundle and reloads the page, but the image URL and content are still the old ones.

Only restarting the dev server serves the new image. Without `bundledDev`, the same steps work.

Other ways of referencing an image are not affected. After the same swap, images referenced with `new URL('./img.png', import.meta.url)`, with CSS `url()`, or from `public/` are served with the new content.

I checked this by fetching the page, the bundle and the assets straight from the dev server, so browser caching is not involved.

This may share a root cause with the `not inlined assets HMR` test that is skipped under bundled dev in #23028 (tracked in rolldown/rolldown#10962). That entry covers the missing HMR update. This report adds that the stale asset also survives a full reload and a rebuild of its importer, so it stays stale until the server is restarted.


### Reproduction

https://github.com/ArturiusInc/vite-bundleddev-stale-image

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

1. Open the page. All four images are red.
2. In a second terminal, run `npm run swap`. It overwrites each image in place (same file name) with a blue version.
3. Reload the page.

| Referenced as | Expected | Actual |

| `import url from './img-import.png'` | blue | **red** (same URL, old content) |

### Describe the bug

Vite serves a file from outside its root through `/@fs/`. Vite sees the first `git checkout` of that file. After that, Vite does not see changes to the file until the server restarts. This includes an edit in place. Files inside the root do not have this problem.

I traced it on Linux with ext4:

1. For a file outside the root, [`ensureWatchedFile`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/v8.3.5/packages/vite/src/node/utils.ts#L785-L801) calls `watcher.add(file)`. chokidar watches only that file, not its folder.
2. `git checkout` removes the file and creates a new file. ext4 gives the new file the same inode number.

_Investigated and written with the help of an AI coding agent (Claude); reproduced locally._

### Describe the bug

When a file that the dev server has transformed is deleted, its module node stays in `urlToModuleMap`, `idToModuleMap` and `fileToModulesMap` (with its `transformResult`) for the life of the server. `onFileDelete` only removes the module from its importees' `importers`.

A re-created path reuses its node, so the graph grows by one node per *distinct* deleted path: renames, generated files, branch switches. In a long dev session with file-based routing (routes added, renamed, removed) this is a steady leak while the number of live files stays constant.

The repro runs 200 cycles of: create `src/gen/mod-<i>.js`, import it from `src/entry.js`, transform both, delete it, wait for the watcher's `unlink`. At most two files exist at any time.

```
cycle=   0 liveFiles=1 idToModuleMap=1 urlToModuleMap=1 fileToModulesMap=1 heapUsed=13.4MB
cycle= 100 liveFiles=1 idToModuleMap=101 urlToModuleMap=101 fileToModulesMap=101 heapUsed=14.7MB
cycle= 200 liveFiles=1 idToModuleMap=201 urlToModuleMap=201 fileToModulesMap=201 heapUsed=15.1MB
```

### Describe the bug

Since 8.3.0-beta.0, a nested worker (`new Worker(new URL('./helper.js', import.meta.url))` inside a worker) is sometimes left out of `dist/`, while the outer worker chunk still points at `/assets/helper-<hash>.js`. So it 404s at runtime. The build itself doesn't warn or fail.

This happens when the module that starts the nested worker (`lib.js`) is **also part of the main bundle's module graph but gets tree-shaken there** (only reachable through an unused export), while the outer worker really uses it:

```
main.js ──> index.js ──> start.js:  new Worker(new URL('./outer.worker.js', import.meta.url))
                    └──> driver.js ──> lib.js   (unused export, tree-shaken from main)
outer.worker.js ──> lib.js:  new Worker(new URL('./helper.js', import.meta.url))
```

Result:
- 8.2.4: `helper-9ko3iLT2.js`, `index-*.js` and `outer.worker-6EdLO_Ut.js` are all emitted.
- 8.3.0-beta.0 / 8.3.5: `outer.worker-6EdLO_Ut.js` references `assets/helper-9ko3iLT2.js`, but that file is not emitted.

If `driver.js` is removed from `index.js` (so `lib.js` is never in the main graph), 8.3.5 emits `helper.js` correctly.

Swapping Rolldown versions doesn't change it (vite 8.3.5 + rolldown 1.2.4 breaks; vite 8.2.4 + rolldown 1.2.14 works), so it looks like a change on the Vite side between 8.2.x and 8.3.0-beta.0. It might be the worker output cache: the nested worker is built for the main bundle, where its reference is tree-shaken away, and is then reused by the outer worker build without being emitted there. That's a guess, though. #22888 (asset URLs via `import.meta.ROLLDOWN_FILE_URL_*`) and #23848 / #23874 (nested worker build caching) touch nearby code.

Real-world case: `@evolu/web` declares `"sideEffects": []` and re-exports a SQLite driver module that is tree-shaken from the app bundle, while its DB worker uses `@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm` (via `@evolu/sqlite-wasm`). sqlite-wasm starts `sqlite3-opfs-async-proxy.js` and `sqlite3-worker1-bundler-friendly.mjs` as nested workers. On 8.3.x both are missing from `dist/`, so the database fails to start in production.

https://gist.github.com/dearkafka/7f65337c045a0dc63576064b87d2c377

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
npm install
npm run build       # vite build && node check.mjs
# 8.3.5 -> MISSING (referenced by outer.worker-6EdLO_Ut.js): helper-9ko3iLT2.js
npx vite@8.2.4 build && node check.mjs
```

### Description

When vite's module runner loads a module, the server sends the code back with the source map appended as a base64 comment (`inlineSourceMap` in `packages/vite/src/node/ssr/fetchModule.ts`). The runner keeps that whole string as `meta.code` and the evaluator hands all of it to v8.

The comment is often as big as the code. V8 scans every byte of it on compile, and it sits in memory for the life of the module.

With `sourcemapInterceptor: 'prepareStackTrace'` the only thing in vite that reads the comment is `getModuleSourceMapById`, and it reads it out of `meta.code`, not out of what v8 compiled.

On a private 100 file typescript backend suite under vitest, 8 workers, leaving just the comment out of what v8 compiles cut wall time about 4.6% (95% interval 2.4 to 6.5) and cpu 4.5%.

I'd like to send a PR for this. Branch is ready:
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/compare/main...maschwenk:vite:feat/module-runner-separate-source-map

### Suggested solution

Send the map as data next to the code instead of inside it.

- `FetchFunctionOptions.separateSourceMap?: boolean`. When set, `fetchModule` returns the map in a new optional `ViteFetchResult.map` and leaves it out of `code`. `//# sourceURL` stays in `code` since stack frames get the file name from it, and `startOffset` applies to the map as it does today.
- `ModuleRunnerOptions.separateSourceMap?: boolean`, default `false`. The runner sends the flag unless `sourcemapInterceptor` is `'node'`, because node reads the inline comment itself.
- `getModuleSourceMapById` uses `meta.map` when it's there and falls back to the comment.

Compatibility:

- Old runners don't send the flag and get inline code.
- Old servers ignore the flag, so `map` is missing and the runner reads the comment.
- `remoteRunner.inlineSourceMap: false` still wins: no map either way.
- Externalized and cached results don't change. Invalidation already clears `meta` and `map`, so hmr picks up the new map.
- Runners share the transform result. Inline mode writes the map into it; the separate path doesn't, and drops a map an inline-mode runner already appended.

It's opt-in rather than the default for `'prepareStackTrace'` because a debugger attached to the process reads the map from the comment in the compiled script. Without it, breakpoints land in generated code.

Vitest asks `fetchModule` for code without a map and appends its own, so it would fill `map` itself to benefit. The vitest issue for the same problem:

- https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11717

### Alternative

Strip the comment in the evaluator right before compile. Smaller change, but the server still builds and sends the base64 string and the runner still has to search for it.

### Additional context

Related, faster extraction of the inline map:

- https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/23775

### Describe the bug

Since the Rolldown-based dependency scanner, a dynamic `import()` inside a function that the scanned module never references is not crawled. Dependencies of the imported module are not pre-bundled at startup. Vite 7's esbuild scanner did crawl them.

This matters for single-file components. The scanner sees only the `<script>` block, so a function used only in the template (an event handler, a Svelte action or `{@attach}`, a Vue `@click`) looks unreferenced. Its lazily imported modules' dependencies are then found only when the browser first requests them. That triggers `new dependencies optimized` and `optimized dependencies changed. reloading`. In a SvelteKit app, that reload raced with a page that was still loading. The page mixed two copies of the Svelte runtime chunk and failed with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'call')` in `get_first_child`.

### Reproduction

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro && mkdir src
echo '{ "name": "repro", "private": true, "type": "module" }' > package.json
printf '<!doctype html>\n<script type="module" src="/src/main.js"></script>\n' > index.html
# never called in this module: in a Svelte/Vue component, a handler only the template uses
echo "const load = () => import('./lazy.js')" > src/main.js
printf "import { nanoid } from 'nanoid'\nexport default nanoid\n" > src/lazy.js
npm install vite@8 nanoid@5
npx vite --force
# in a second shell: cat node_modules/.vite/deps/_metadata.json, then request the module
curl -s localhost:5173/src/lazy.js > /dev/null
```

| | Vite 7.3.7 | Vite 8.3.5 |
|---|---|---|
| `optimized` in `_metadata.json` after startup | `nanoid` | (empty) |
| on requesting `/src/lazy.js` | nothing new | `dependency optimized: nanoid` |

With Vite 8.3.5 the dependency is found at startup when the function is exported (`export const load = () => import('./lazy.js')`), when it is referenced (`window.addEventListener('click', load)`), or when `import('./lazy.js')` is at the top level. Only the unreferenced case misses it.

My guess, not verified in Rolldown's source: the scan drops unreferenced code before collecting dynamic imports.

### Expected behavior

The scanner crawls `import()` calls wherever they appear, as Vite 7 did, so dependencies reachable from component scripts are pre-bundled at startup.

### Workaround

List the affected dependencies in `optimizeDeps.include`.

### System info

Vite 8.3.5 (also via vite-plus 1.4.0, which bundles it), Node 24.22.1, macOS (arm64). Related but separate: #23669 / #23678, where `.svelte` files in `node_modules` weren't recorded after the Rolldown migration.

### Describe the bug

While working on the yak integration for qwik I stumbled upon an issue where HMR is not triggered:

![color.txt changes from hotpink to lightblue. The Vite plugin calls addWatchFile("color.txt") in load, but Vite sends no HMR update, so the box in the browser stays hotpink, expected lightblue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jantimon/vite-load-addwatchfile/main/hmr.gif)

So I created this minimal reproduction where a mini plugin makes the virtual stylesheet `/color.css` from `color.txt` and calls `this.addWatchFile("color.txt")` in `load`

In qwik and other SSR scenarios `index.html` loads that virtual css with a `<link>` not via JS imports

Now I would expect that once `color.txt` is edited Vite would trigger an HMR update for `/color.css`

However `_updateModuleLoadAddedImports` keeps the files from `load` only if the module node already exists ([pluginContainer.ts#L215-L218](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/v8.3.5/packages/vite/src/node/server/pluginContainer.ts#L215-L218)). 

`loadAndTransform` calls `load` at [L269](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/v8.3.5/packages/vite/src/node/server/transformRequest.ts#L269) and creates the node afterwards at [L354](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/v8.3.5/packages/vite/src/node/server/transformRequest.ts#L354)

So on the first request of a module the files from `load` are dropped

Maybe nobody ran into this as a stylesheet imported from JS does not hit this as for theses cases Vite creates its node while it analyzes the importer

Creating the node before `load` seems to fix it for my reproduction:

```diff
+ mod ??= await moduleGraph._ensureEntryFromUrl(url, undefined, resolved)
  const loadResult = await pluginContainer.load(id)
```

Calling `addWatchFile` in `transform` instead also works because the node exists by then

`addWatchFile` in `load` is supported since #14967 (which fixed #3474), and the [environment API guide](https://vite.dev/guide/api-environment-frameworks) calls it from `load`

@bluwy found this case in #18103 and added a failing test for it:

> The `module` does not exist until the `load` hook finishes

He closed the PR with:

> Probably still an issue, but no one seems to have reported this so it's probably not important enough to fix this. Also, it's easier to track this in an issue.

So here you go 😄 this is that issue

### Describe the bug

If two workers both start the same nested worker, `vite build` can bundle that nested worker twice. The output is the same both times, so the second build is wasted work.

This happens when the two parent workers are bundled at the same time. `bundleWorkerEntry` only checks the cache for worker bundles that have already *finished*:

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/467f7ac3b8c7cca0b33290e7fd86f3fc79ce92cb/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L339-L342

So when the second parent asks for the nested worker while the first build of it is still running, the cache misses and a second build starts.

In a small app this costs nothing. In our app (18 workers, a few of which start other workers) it caused 38 worker builds instead of 24, each with 1,400+ modules. Removing the duplicates cut the CPU time of `vite build` by about 40%, with byte-identical output.

I'm happy to send a PR.

### Reproduction

The files are below. I can put them in a repo if that's easier.

`index.html`

```html
<script type="module" src="/src/main.js"></script>
```

`src/main.js`

```js
import './start-a.js'
import './start-b.js'
```

`src/start-a.js` (`start-b.js` is the same, with `b.js`)

```js
new Worker(new URL('./a.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })
```

`src/a.js` and `src/b.js` (identical)

```js
new Worker(new URL('./shared.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })
```

`src/shared.js`

```js
console.log('shared worker')
```

`vite.config.js`

```js
import path from 'node:path'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

// Logs every worker bundle Vite starts.
const logWorkerBuilds = () => ({
  name: 'log-worker-builds',
  buildStart(options) {
    console.log('bundling worker:', [options.input].flat().map(id => path.basename(id)).join())
  },
})

export default defineConfig({
  worker: { format: 'es', plugins: () => [logWorkerBuilds()] },
})
```

The two spawns need to be in separate modules (`start-a.js`, `start-b.js`). If they are in the same file, Vite bundles `a.js` and `b.js` one after the other and the cache works.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install vite@8.3.4`
2. `npx vite build`

Expected: `shared.js` is bundled once.

```
bundling worker: b.js
bundling worker: a.js
bundling worker: shared.js
```

Actual: `shared.js` is bundled twice (every run). Only one `shared-*.js` file ends up in `dist`.

```
bundling worker: b.js
bundling worker: a.js
bundling worker: shared.js
bundling worker: shared.js
```

### Possible fix

Keep the in-progress build in the cache too, so a second request waits for it instead of starting another one. Roughly:

```ts
const bundleInfo = workerOutput.getWorkerBundle(input)
if (bundleInfo) return bundleInfo

let pending = workerOutput.pendingBundles.get(input)
if (!pending) {
  pending = buildWorkerBundle(config, input) // the existing body of bundleWorkerEntry
    .finally(() => workerOutput.pendingBundles.delete(input))
  workerOutput.pendingBundles.set(input, pending)
}
return pending
```

The existing circular-import check has to run before this, otherwise `a -> b -> a` would wait on itself instead of throwing the current error.

### Description

A render through the module runner fetches a module only when evaluation reaches its import. Each module costs one `fetchModule` round trip, one after another. Each later import of a module the runner has already evaluated costs another round trip, which only answers `{ cache: true }`.

This matters when the runner talks to the server over a slow link. `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` bundles this runner into workerd and sends `fetchModule` over HTTP. On a TanStack Start app, with every transform already in Vite's module graph, a page that loads 1,035 modules took 935 ms to render. Node sat idle for 88% of that time while the runner waited on round trips. With an earlier version of the change below applied as a patch to the plugin's copy of the runner, the same render took 615 ms, and the browser got its HTML at 0.47 s instead of 0.79 s.

I intend to open a PR.

### Suggested solution

In `packages/vite/src/module-runner/runner.ts`:

1. When the runner receives a module's code, it reads the `__vite_ssr_import__("…")` calls that `ssrTransform` writes for static imports, and fetches those modules, at most 16 at a time, while the module evaluates. The import that needs a module joins the request in flight through `concurrentModuleNodePromises`.
2. With HMR on, the runner counts HMR messages. A module the server sent or confirmed since the last message that can mean a change is used again without a request. `runner.import()` keeps asking the server, so a change the server makes without an HMR message still reaches the runner through the entry.

Without HMR the runner keeps today's behaviour, since nothing would tell it that a module changed. `ssrLoadModule` runs its runner with `hmr: false`, so it is not affected.

### Alternative

The server could return each module's import list from `fetchModule`, so the runner would not scan code. That changes the transport protocol, and a runner bundled into another tool can talk to a different Vite version, so I'd keep this on the runner side.

### Additional context

#22079 and #22081 are about bare specifiers in the runner's URL cache. This proposal only reuses or prefetches URLs that start with `/`, which the server resolves the same way for every importer, so it does not add to that problem.

Claude Code wrote this issue and the change it proposes. I haven't reviewed the code in depth yet.

### Describe the bug

When the first line of `index.html` holds two module scripts with nothing else before the second one, `vite build` bundles both modules but removes only the first original `<script>` tag. The second original tag stays in `dist/index.html`, so the page also requests `/b.js`, which is not in `dist` (404). If that tag ends the file, its final `>` is cut off as well.

Cause, in `nodeStartWithLeadingWhitespace` (`packages/vite/src/node/plugins/html.ts`, unchanged on `main`):

```ts
const lineStartOffset = startOffset - node.sourceCodeLocation!.startCol
// ...
const line = s.slice(Math.max(0, lineStartOffset), startOffset)
isLineEmpty = !line.trim()
// ...
return isLineEmpty ? lineStartOffset : startOffset
```

parse5's `startCol` is 1-based, so for a node on line 1 `lineStartOffset` is `-1`. The first script on that line has already been removed from `s`, so the sliced prefix is empty and the function returns the unclamped `-1`. `s.remove(-1, endOffset)` then counts from the end of the string (magic-string accepts negative indices), so it removes `[length - 1, endOffset)`: only the final `>` when the tag ends the file, and nothing when a newline follows. Returning `Math.max(0, lineStartOffset)` would fix it. Stylesheet `<link>` removal uses the same helper.

### Reproduction

Inline minimal reproduction below (three files, no config).

### Steps to reproduce

1. `index.html`, a single line with no trailing newline:

   ```html
   <script type="module" src="/a.js"></script><script type="module" src="/b.js"></script>
   ```

2. `a.js`: `console.log('module a')` and `b.js`: `console.log('module b')`
3. Run `vite build` (no config file, no plugins).

`dist/index.html`:

```html
<script type="module" crossorigin src="/assets/index-QgGPn3yV.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="/b.js"></script
```

Both modules are in `dist/assets/index-*.js`; `dist/b.js` does not exist.

| `index.html` | second original tag in `dist/index.html` |
| --- | --- |
| adjacent tags on line 1, no trailing newline | kept, final `>` missing |
| adjacent tags on line 1, trailing newline | kept |
| newline between the tags | removed |
| same tags in a one-line `<!doctype html><html><head></head><body>...</body></html>` | removed |

parse5 reports correct offsets in every case (with Vite's bundled parse5: `/a.js` at 0-43, `/b.js` at 43-86).

```Shell
Vite 8.3.4 (the same output on 8.3.1)
Node 24.19.0
Windows 11 Pro, win32 x64 10.0.26300
```

bun

### Describe the bug

Once the dev server stops, every `import.meta.hot.send()` call logs an error in the browser:

```
[vite] SendBeforeConnectError: send was called before connect
```

The message is wrong: `send` was called *after* the client had connected and then lost the server. Nothing has gone wrong in the app, and the message cannot be delivered or acted on, so it is noise. The client is already showing `server connection lost. Polling for restart...` and will reload the page once the server is back.

The error comes from `send()` in `packages/vite/src/shared/moduleRunnerTransport.ts`. After a disconnect, `isConnected` is `false` and `connectingPromise` is `undefined`, so it throws:

```ts
async send(data) {
  if (!invokeableTransport.send) return
  if (!isConnected) {
    if (connectingPromise) {
      await connectingPromise
    } else {
      throw new SendBeforeConnectError('send was called before connect')
    }
  }
  await invokeableTransport.send(data)
},
```

`HMRClient.send` catches the rejection and passes it to `logger.error`, which is `console.error("[vite]", err)`.

This gets much worse when an app forwards browser console output to the dev server through `hot.send`. That is a common pattern for dev logging, and it is how we found this. Each forwarded line fails, the failure is logged with `console.error`, and that log is forwarded again. The rejection arrives in a later microtask, so a plain re-entrancy guard around the send does not stop it. The tab ends up at 100% CPU until it is closed.

Possible fixes:

- drop `send` calls quietly while disconnected (the page reloads on reconnect anyway), or
- queue them until the next connection, or
- at least give the error a message that is true after a disconnect, such as "send was called while disconnected".

### Reproduction

https://github.com/shkumbinhasani/vite-hot-send-repro

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm install`
2. `npm run dev`, then open http://localhost:5199
3. The page calls `import.meta.hot.send("repro:ping", …)` once a second.
4. Stop the dev server with Ctrl+C.
5. Look at the browser console: `[vite] SendBeforeConnectError: send was called before connect` once a second, forever.

`main.js` in full:

```js
let sends = 0;
setInterval(() => {
  sends++;
  document.getElementById("count").textContent = `sends: ${sends}`;
  import.meta.hot?.send("repro:ping", { sends });
}, 1000);
```

```
[vite] server connection lost. Polling for restart...
[vite] SendBeforeConnectError: send was called before connect
[vite] SendBeforeConnectError: send was called before connect
[vite] SendBeforeConnectError: send was called before connect
```

### Description

When Vite encounters a CSS url() reference that cannot be resolved during a production build, it emits a warning and leaves the URL unchanged for resolution at runtime.

This is useful when resources are intentionally unavailable at build time, but it also means that typos in local asset paths can go unnoticed until runtime, where they result in 404 requests.

Currently, there does not appear to be a supported configuration option to control the severity of these unresolved URLs.

### Suggested solution

I would like a configuration option to control whether unresolved CSS asset URLs produce a warning or an error.

My preference would be for unresolved local assets to fail the build by default, since this catches mistakes early and provides better feedback during development. However, I understand that some users intentionally rely on the current behavior because not all resources are available at build time.

Keeping the current default for backward compatibility would be reasonable. Perhaps changing the default in a future major release could also be considered.

Ideally, the resulting diagnostic would retain the relevant source location and provide a useful error message.

### Alternative

There are workarounds for changing this behavior, but they are hacky and unreliable. For example, intercepting the warning through a custom logger and turning it into an error requires matching the warning message and can result in poor error reporting, including missing or invalid source locations.

I recognize the concern about adding yet another configuration option. However, since the current behavior serves a legitimate use case, simply changing the default may not be sufficient for everyone. A first-class option to control the severity would let users choose the behavior that fits their project, while a smarter default could be considered for a future major release.

### Additional context

Thank you for all your work on Vite! I'd be happy to contribute a PR implementing this if the maintainers agree that this would be a useful addition.

### Describe the bug

When we have a framework and then plugins that utilize the framework, the plugin essentially requires these `optimizeDeps.exclude` entries. Otherwise, it's referencing essentially two instances of the same thing. Changing the import extension makes it work. Adding more exclusions feels like a workaround rather than fixing the original issue upstream.

The minimal reproduction isolates the exact trigger: an optimized plugin imports `state-lib/component.vue`, which resolves through package exports to `component.vue.js`. That file re-exports a reader from `./client.js`. **`state-lib` is already in `optimizeDeps.exclude`**, but the component's reader gets bundled into the optimized plugin instead of sharing the original module.

The plugin's direct `state-lib/client` import shares the initialized client. Its component import returns `undefined`. Changing only the import name to `state-lib/component.js`, mapped to the exact same file, fixes it. An early `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.external` predicate also fixes it.

The reproduction uses only Vite and two generated ESM packages. There is no Vue plugin, actual Vue SFC, application framework, alias or symlink.

| Vite | Rolldown | Excluded `.vue` export | Same file through `.js` export | Early external rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8.0.16 | 1.0.3 | Separate state | Shared state | Shared state |
| 8.3.4 | 1.2.14 | Separate state | Shared state | Shared state |

Vite 8.3.4 was npm's `latest` release when checked on 2026-10-16. Both versions were tested with the final reproduction script and explicit exit-code capture.

Separate checks, not included in the minimal package: registering `@vitejs/plugin-vue` 6.0.5 or 6.0.10 with Vue 3.5.32 produces the same failure on both Vite versions. A Vite 8.3.4 dev-server run in headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 also reproduces the failure and both passing controls, with no page errors. That browser check does not call the standalone `optimizeDeps()` API.

### Describe the bug With `experimental.bundledDev`, nothing is ever removed from `BundledDev.memoryFiles` until the server closes. - `storeOutputFiles` only calls `memoryFiles.set`. - `getRolldownOptions` forces `chunkFileNames: 'assets/[name]-[hash].js'` and `assetFileNames: 'assets/[name]-[hash][extname]'`. So every rebuild that changes a chunk stores it, and its source map, under a new name, next to all the previous copies. HMR patches (`hmr_patch_N.js` + `.map`) are never removed either. Every old file stays served. There are two ways to hit it. 1. **A chunk shared between entries** (multiple `rolldownOptions.input` entries, or `devMode: { lazy: false }` with dynamic imports). Each edit to a module in a shared chunk adds that chunk and its map again, plus every hashed chunk that imports it, because the hash change cascades. In our app, with ~230 entries, 20 edits to a module most entries import took `memoryFiles` from 1,919 to 28,479 files, and the process RSS from 3.9 GB to 12.1 GB. 2. **The default config with a page open.** Each edit adds `hmr_patch_N.js` and `hmr_patch_N.js.map`. That's slower growth, but it's unbounded for a long-running session. **Expected:** `memoryFiles` holds the latest build output, plus the patches that are still pending. **Actual:** it holds every file ever emitted. `storeOutputFiles` has `// NOTE: don't clear memoryFiles here as incremental build reuses the files`. In the reproduction, though, each rebuild hands `storeOutputFiles` the complete output, unchanged entries included. A possible fix: - Remember the previous output's file names, and delete the ones the new output does not contain. - Delete an HMR patch or lazy payload once the client reports it delivered (`vite:bundled-dev:payload-delivered`), or keep only the last few. A workaround for build output, not for HMR patches: a plugin that removes the hash, so each rebuild overwrites the same keys: ```js { name: 'unhashed-dev-chunks', outputOptions: options => ({ ...options, chunkFileNames: 'assets/[name].js', assetFileNames: 'assets/[name][extname]' }), } ``` ### Reproduction https://github.com/asapach/vite-issue-memoryfiles ### Steps to reproduce **Case 1, a chunk shared between two entries** (scripted): 1. `npm install` 2. `npm run repro` The script uses `bundledDev.memoryFiles` and `devEngine` internals only to count the files and to wait for each rebuild deterministically. ### Description

On Windows, the first time a process listens on a wildcard address, Windows Defender Firewall asks "Do you want to allow public and private networks to access this app? Node.js JavaScript Runtime". A Vite dev server configured to stay on loopback (`server.host: '127.0.0.1'`) still brings that prompt on a fresh machine, because `httpServerStart` calls `isPortAvailable(port)` on every start, `strictPort` included, and `isPortAvailable` opens and closes a listener on `0.0.0.0` and `::`.

So a person who never asked for network access is asked to grant it, and one who answers Allow opens Node to the network for nothing. Observed with Astro 7.3.8's `astro dev` (host 127.0.0.1, port 4321) on Vite 8.3.4: the only non-loopback sockets during start were `0.0.0.0:4321` and `[::]:4321`, for a moment, about 5 s in. When it ran from a session with no desktop, Windows silently added "Block" rules for node.exe instead.

### Suggested solution

Skip the wildcard probe when `server.host` is a loopback address, since nothing on a wildcard address can then be reached through the configured host anyway. Or, with `strictPort`, let the bind itself be the answer, and probe the wildcard addresses with a connect rather than a listen when the warning about a server on a wildcard IP is wanted.

### Alternative

Document the prompt for Windows users, and that Cancel is the right answer for a loopback-only dev server.

### Additional context

Windows 11 ARM64 (build 26300), Node 22.23.3, Vite 8.3.4 (through Astro 7.3.8), npm 10.9.9. The code is in `dist/node` around `httpServerStart` / `isPortAvailable` / `tryListen`.

I searched the existing issues for this (firewall, wildcard port check) and found none.

---

### Describe the bug

Starting the dev server crashes during dependency optimization:

```
Error during dependency optimization:

Cannot destructure property 'exportsData' of depForEntryFileName[chunk.fileName] as it is undefined
    at .../vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:28633:14
```

This happens when two pre-bundled entries resolve such that one entry's imported module
is itself another optimizer entry: Rolldown emits a second entry chunk for the shared
module and disambiguates the file name with a `2` suffix (`effect_Schema2.js`), but Vite
builds `depForEntryFileName` keys as `flattenId(dep.id) + '.js'`, so the suffixed chunk
name is not found and the destructuring throws. The crashing chunk has
`isEntry === true` and the same `facadeModuleId` as the real entry chunk.


## Workarounds tried

- `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['effect/schema']` avoids the crash, but leaves a raw
  copy of the effect graph next to the pre-bundled copies in dev.
- `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions: { preserveEntrySignatures: 'strict' }` → still crashes.
- `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions: { preserveEntrySignatures: false }` → still crashes.
- Same crash on `vite@8.3.2` (rolldown 1.2.11) and `vite@8.3.4` (rolldown 1.2.13),
  so this is not a regression from a recent Vite/rolldown bump.

## Expected behavior

Either handle the disambiguated entry chunk file names in the optimizer bookkeeping (or
map by `facadeModuleId`), or emit a descriptive error. Related past reports with the same
crash for other causes: #21885 (`+` in subpaths), #22198 (`$` in subpaths).

# Dependency optimizer recreates cache directories after `server.close()` resolves — Vite 8.1.2 and 8.3.4

## Reproduction

https://gist.github.com/raskum1984/dc5bacb0a0f9ff804236e7e0cbc12966

Download/clone all nine files, then follow README.md:

```sh
node setup.mjs
npm ci --prefix baseline
npm ci --prefix candidate
node run.mjs baseline
node run.mjs candidate
```

## Expected behavior

After `await server.close()` resolves, and a test-owned cache directory has been
removed, Vite should not recreate optimizer output inside that directory.

## Actual behavior

Two concurrent middleware-mode Vite servers use independent caches. Both Vite
8.1.2 and 8.3.4 successfully load a simple React SSR module and resolve their
original `close()` calls. Each owned cache is then removed successfully; the
child logs an empty cache-root snapshot. The child exits naturally with code 0.

Inspection by the parent after child exit finds recreated `server-*/deps_temp_*`
directories containing `react.js`, `react-dom_server.js`, sourcemaps and Rolldown
runtime output. The parent exits 1 to report this lifecycle failure; it does not
force child termination or suppress an error.

This occurred in three earlier isolated runs per version, affecting six caches
per version, and in two further public-reproduction checks per version,
including a check after installation using `npm ci`.

## Environment

- macOS ARM64
- Node.js 24.21.0
- npm 11.19.0
- Baseline: Vite 8.1.2, Rolldown 1.1.3, Darwin ARM64 binding 1.1.3
- Candidate: Vite 8.3.4, normal transitive Rolldown 1.2.13, binding 1.2.13
- React and react-dom 19.2.7

## Additional context

An original larger test suite intermittently experienced `ENOTEMPTY` during
test-owned cache removal after Vite's original `close()` resolved. Separate
native worker crashes were observed, but their connection to this lifecycle is
unconfirmed. This minimal reproduction demonstrates late cache output; it does
not itself reproduce the original `ENOTEMPTY` or native crash.

There are no sleeps, cleanup retries, shared cache, optimizer disabling or
concurrency reduction. Each attempt has a fresh cache root and child process.
The reproduction contains only synthetic code and locked dependencies, with no
application configuration, credentials or external service access.

### Describe the bug

With `css.transformer: 'lightningcss'`, importing the same CSS Module normally and with `?inline` produces different class names:

```js
import classes from './badge.module.css'
import css from './badge.module.css?inline'

css.includes(`.${classes.badge}`) // false
```

The processed CSS string should contain the class exported by the normal import. `compileLightningCSS` removes `?direct` from the filename passed to Lightning CSS, but keeps `?inline`. That query becomes part of the path used to generate the module names.

### Describe the bug

When a file is saved twice less than 50ms apart, `server.watcher` emits `change` for the first save only. The second save is never reported, so HMR and SSR keep the stale content until the next unrelated save.

This comes from chokidar 3's per-path `change` throttle, which drops events inside the 50ms window with no trailing emit. It's a known chokidar issue ([#1084](https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1084), [#1455](https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1455)). It's fixed on chokidar `main` for v6, where the suppressed change is replayed when the window closes, but v6 isn't released yet, and 4.0.3 and 5.0.0 still drop it. Vite is still on chokidar `^3.6.0` (after the #18659 revert).

> [!NOTE]
> `chokidar` v6 was released on Oct. 19 2026

body:
### Describe the bug

With `@vitejs/plugin-legacy`, the CSS minifier removes vendor prefixes that Safari and Firefox need.

```css
/* input */
.a { -webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none; }

/* output with legacy() */
.a{user-select:none}
```

Safari only supports `-webkit-user-select`, so this rule does nothing in any Safari, modern or legacy bundle.

**Why:** plugin-legacy sets `build.cssTarget` to `'chrome61'` ([source](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/plugin-legacy/src/index.ts)). Its comment says only `HexRGBA` affects the minified output. That was true for esbuild. Since Vite 8 the default CSS minifier is Lightning CSS, which also uses the target to decide which vendor prefixes to keep. With Chrome 61 as the only target, it drops every prefix Chrome 61 does not need.

Other prefixes lost the same way: `-webkit-hyphens` (Safari < 17), `position: -webkit-sticky` (Safari < 13), `-moz-user-select` (Firefox < 69), `-moz-appearance` (Firefox < 80).

**Suggested fix:** keep `chrome61` and add the browsers from the plugin's `targets`, converted with `browserslist-to-esbuild` as `modernTargets` already is. Keep `chrome61` in the list: Lightning CSS also rewrites `rgba()` into `#RRGGBBAA` when the target allows it.

**Workaround:** set `build.cssTarget` yourself, for example `['chrome61', 'safari12']`. Setting `css.lightningcss.targets` does not help, because `build.cssTarget` takes precedence.

Related: #21139, where `chrome61` was explained as making the CSS work in Safari 15. That holds for syntax, not for prefixes.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/puckey/vite-legacy-css-prefixes

```sh
npm install
npm run repro
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. `vite build` with `plugins: [legacy()]` and the CSS above
2. Read the CSS in `dist/assets/`: `-webkit-user-select` is gone

| Config | Output |
|---|---|
| `legacy()` | `.a{user-select:none}` |
| `legacy()` + `build.cssTarget: ['chrome61', 'safari12']` | `.a{-webkit-user-select:none;user-select:none}` |
| no plugin-legacy | `.a{-webkit-user-select:none;user-select:none}` |

body:
### Description

I'm building a library that's intended to only run in the Node environment. Using `build.lib` and `build.target` set to a Node version, Vite still builds the library for the browser. It replaces Node built-ins such as `fs/promises`, `node:crypto` and `events` with `__vite-browser-external`, and it prints this warning:

> Module "fs/promises" has been externalized for browser compatibility

The build output then fails at runtime, or the build fails with an error like `"randomUUID" is not exported by "__vite-browser-external"`.

A maintainer explained the cause in #18918. A plain `vite build` builds only the client environment. The `target` value does not change the environment. To get a Node build, the user must move the library configuration to `environments.ssr`:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  environments: {
    client: {
      consumer: 'server'
    },
    ssr: {}
  }
})
```

This works, but feels like a hacky workaround, as the library is unrelated to SSR. The documentation for `build.lib` also doesn't mention this. #13953 asks the same question for a Node backend build, and it has no answer since July 2023.

### Suggested solution

One of these changes would help:

1. If `build.lib` is set and `build.target` names only Node versions (for example `node18`), Vite builds for Node and avoids externalized stubs.
2. Vite adds an option for Node library builds, for example `build.lib.platform: 'node'`.

### Alternative

_No response_

### Additional context

Related issues/discussions: #18915 / #18918, #13953

### Describe the bug

During development we keep our worktrees inside the `.git` directory, e.g. `<repoRoot>/.git/.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`. Worktrees under `<repoRoot>/.claude/*` get deleted by the `git clean` commands our agent is allowed to run as part of the workflow, and keeping them in `.git` avoids that.

The Vite dev server doesn't work with projects like this: every request gets a 403, and changes don't trigger HMR.

The reason is that the default `**/.git/**` patterns (in `server.fs.deny` and in the watcher's ignore list, `server.watch.ignored`) are matched against the absolute path. Working around it with `!**/.git/**` also un-ignores `node_modules`, because the negation overrides the default ignores.

I'd expect the `.git` exclusion patterns to apply to `.git` directories themselves, not to the directory the project lives in.

Relevant code:
- [`server.fs.deny` default](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/cf5c0288d526824aead1b24e977400f13c527927/packages/vite/src/node/server/index.ts#L1241)
- [watcher default ignore](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/cf5c0288d526824aead1b24e977400f13c527927/packages/vite/src/node/watch.ts#L79)

### Reproduction

https://github.com/cainrus/vite-dev-inside-git-dir

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
npm install
npm run setup   # copies ./app into .git/inside/app
```

| command | `GET /` | edit `main.js` | edit `node_modules/fake-pkg/index.js` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm run dev:outside` (control) | 200 | HMR | ignored |
| `npm run dev:inside` | 403 | nothing | ignored |
| `npm run dev:inside:opt-in` (`fs.deny` without `**/.git/**` + `watch.ignored: ['!**/.git/**']`) | 200 | HMR | picked up |
| `npm run dev:inside:narrow` (same, with a negation that skips `node_modules`, see `app/vite.config.js`) | 200 | HMR | ignored |

body:
### Describe the bug

I am using colons in some paths for auto-generated files (using Laravel Wayfinder), which contain colons in route file names. These  imports fail, because vite rejects any path with a colon in it.

Since #22572, isFileLoadingAllowed rejects any path that contains `:` while `server.fs.strict` is on. The check runs on every OS, but `:` is a valid character in file and folder names on Linux and macOS.

On 8.3.1 this breaks:

- Dynamic imports. `import('./route:name/index.js')` gets a 403. Static imports still work, but only because import analysis pre-transforms them with `warmupRequest`, which skips the check.
- Projects in a folder with `:` in its name. Every file returns 403, including index.html.
- Vitest's jsdom and happy-dom environments. Vitest turns pre-transform off, so static imports fail too. I reported it in vitest-dev/vitest#11413 and sent a workaround in vitest-dev/vitest#11414. The Vitest maintainers said the fix belongs in Vite.

The server log also says the file is "outside of Vite serving allow list", then lists the folder that contains it.

Like I said, I ran into this with Laravel Wayfinder, which names route folders after route names, for example `routes/company:logo/index.ts`.

The `~` check from the same PR runs only on Windows, but the `:` check runs everywhere, which makes me think whether it was meant to cover NTFS volumes mounted on Linux or macOS?

I have a fix on a branch and I'd like to send a PR:

- Keep rejecting `:` on Windows, where it can never be part of a file name.
- On other OS-es, allow `:`, but also check the path with the stream part removed against `server.fs.deny`. So `.env::$DATA` is checked as `.env` and is still denied.

The trade-off: on an NTFS volume mounted on Linux or macOS, the streams of a file that is allowed and not denied become readable again, as they were before #22572. Would you accept that, or do you prefer a different approach?

I totally get it if you'd like to keep the behavior consistent across different OS-es, but I though this is at least worth a discussion?

### Reproduction

https://github.com/ragulka/vite-colon-path-repro 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction and start the dev server:

body: ### Describe the bug In VS Code, saving a `.vue` file **intermittently does not apply** — the page stays stale and the terminal only prints `(client) [no modules matched]`, with no error, no overlay and nothing in the browser console. It is easy to hit: **commenting/uncommenting a block in the template and saving usually reproduces it within a few saves (2–5)**; the probability grows with the size of the `.vue` (a ~550 KB SFC with a large inline SVG fails on most saves, small components almost never do). **The failure is visible on the page itself**, no tooling needed: the reproduction keeps a yellow banner *inside* the toggled block, at the top of the grid — ```text toggle-block is RENDERED — comment it out and save; if this banner is still here, that save was swallowed ``` Comment the block out, save, and watch the banner: when the update is swallowed the banner (and the whole block) is still rendered, the state counter / component-mount time / on-page HMR event timestamp do not change at all, and the terminal shows only: ```text [DEBUG HMR before-vue] modules: [ "/src/components/HeavyPanel.vue", "/src/components/HeavyPanel.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=c11907fb&lang.css" ] [DEBUG HMR after-vue] modules: [ ] 2026-09-29T07:02:59.014Z vite:hmr (client) [no modules matched] src/components/HeavyPanel.vue 2026-09-29T07:02:59.014Z vite:hmr (ssr) [no modules matched] src/components/HeavyPanel.vue ``` Why: the save is not atomic for a large buffer, so the file is briefly incomplete (or the new bytes are not yet visible) on disk, and Vite's HMR handler fires inside that window. `readModifiedFile()` only retries when the content is *empty*, so plugins can receive a partial or stale copy of the file: ```js async function readModifiedFile(file) { const content = await fsp.readFile(file, 'utf-8') if (!content) { // only retries when the file is *empty* const mtime = (await fsp.stat(file)).mtimeMs for (let n = 0; n < 10; n++) { await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 10)); if ((await fsp.stat(file)).mtimeMs !== mtime) break } return await fsp.readFile(file, 'utf-8') } else return content // half-written content is treated as the whole file } ``` `@vitejs/plugin-vue` caches the descriptor it parsed, so the next event compares the wrong content against its cache, concludes "no change", returns an **empty module list**, and no HMR payload is sent at all (that is the `after-vue: []` / `[no modules matched]` above). **Why file size matters** — the window in which the file is incomplete is the duration of the save, and that grows with the size (plain `fs.writeFile` of the fixture: **0.80 ms @157 KB, 1.96 ms @484 KB, 2.57 ms @918 KB, 5.17 ms @1.8 MB** on this machine; VS Code adds its own I/O, and Windows AV / file-sync can stretch it further). Bigger file → wider window → higher chance the watcher fires inside it. Measured with the reproduction (Vite 8.3.1, one large comment-block toggle per save, saves ~40 ms apart): * **13–14 of 15 saves were swallowed** (`before-vue` has modules, `after-vue` is `[]`, nothing sent over the HMR WebSocket). * Same emulated non-atomic save at other sizes: **157 KB → 14/15**, **484 KB → 14/15**, **918 KB → 12/15**. * In 20 sampled HMR events the file was **mid-write** in **19**, and Vite's own `ctx.read()` returned content that did not match the intended file in **14**. * A single non-chunked write is always fine (`npm run probe:direct` → 0/15), and enabling `server.watch.awaitWriteFinish` → **15/15** fine. Scope: not framework-specific — the truncation happens in Vite's `readModifiedFile()` / watcher pipeline and is file-type agnostic; plugin-vue only makes it *visible* by caching the parsed descriptor. The controlled experiments (`--write=direct` vs `--write=chunked`, `awaitWriteFinish` on/off) point at the read/watch side, not at Vue. Suggested fix: make `readModifiedFile()` retry not only on empty content but while the file is still growing (re-stat until size/mtime are stable), and/or enable `awaitWriteFinish` by default — `server.watch.awaitWriteFinish = { stabilityThreshold: 150, pollInterval: 10 }` makes this reproduction 15/15 green. *(Editor: VS Code `` on Windows 11, plain Ctrl+S saves — `files.autoSave` off. Please fill in the version; that is the only field I could not read from your machine.)* ### Reproduction https://github.com/fullmooooon/vite8-vue-hmr-repro Minimal: only `vite@8.3.1`, `vue@3.5.24`, `@vitejs/plugin-vue@6.0.9` (no other deps), one generated fixture SFC (`src/components/HeavyPanel.vue`, 484 KB by default, size adjustable), no real business or artwork content. **Manual (fastest, ~3 saves):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/fullmooooon/vite8-vue-hmr-repro && cd vite8-vue-hmr-repro && npm install npm run dev # open http://127.0.0.1:5173 ``` Then, in VS Code: click the `+1` button a few times (the state probe at the top), and comment / uncomment the `` wrapper of the **first block inside `.grid`** (search for `reproduction entry`), saving with Ctrl+S a few times. Watch the yellow banner described above. **Automated (same thing, scripted, exits non-zero when it happens):** * `npm run probe` — 15 saves with non-atomic (chunked) writes; exits with code 2 when saves were swallowed. * `npm run probe -- --read-evidence` — same, plus one line per HMR event comparing the file on disk and `ctx.read()` against the intended content. * `npm run probe:fixed` — identical scenario with `server.watch.awaitWriteFinish`: all green (exit 0). * `npm run probe:direct` — identical edits, single write: all green. * Size sweep: `npm run gen -- --cells=N` (1200 ≈ 157 KB, 3700 ≈ 484 KB, 7000 ≈ 918 KB), then repeat. The probe boots the real dev server from the repo's `vite.config.ts`, fetches the page plus the whole import graph over HTTP, subscribes to the real HMR WebSocket, then saves the fixture with a configurable write pattern and records what `before-vue` / `after-vue` saw and which payload reached the client. ### Steps to reproduce 1. `git clone https://github.com/fullmooooon/vite8-vue-hmr-repro && cd vite8-vue-hmr-repro && npm install` 2. `npm run dev`, open http://127.0.0.1:5173, click `+1` a few times. 3. In VS Code open `src/components/HeavyPanel.vue`, comment out the `toggle-block` wrapper (first block inside `.grid`) and press Ctrl+S. Repeat the comment/uncomment toggle and save quickly — a few saves are usually enough. 4. Look at the page: if the yellow banner is still rendered after you commented the block out, that save never reached the client (counter / mount time / HMR-event timestamp all unchanged). Terminal shows `(client) [no modules matched]`. 5. Automated equivalent: `npm run probe` (expect exit code 2, ~13–14 of 15 saves swallowed) and `npm run probe -- --read-evidence` for the raw read proof. 6. Control: `npm run probe:fixed`, or un-comment the `watch: { awaitWriteFinish: … }` line in `vite.config.ts` and repeat step 3 → no more swallowed saves. ### System Info ```shell System: OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200 CPU: (16) x64 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1260P Memory: 5.06 GB / 31.69 GB Binaries: Node: 26.5.1 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE npm: 11.17.0 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD Browsers: Chrome: 154.0.8037.57 Edge: Chromium (152.0.4191.53) Firefox: 146.0.1 - C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe npmPackages: @vitejs/plugin-vue: 6.0.9 => 6.0.9 vite: 8.3.1 => 8.3.1 vue: 3.5.24 => 3.5.24 ``` ### Used Package Manager npm ### Logs `node scripts/hmr-probe.mjs --read-evidence --debug --edits=15` (`DEBUG=vite:hmr`), full log in `probe-output/report.log`: ```text # 1 ok latency=30ms payload=["/src/components/HeavyPanel.vue"] 2026-09-29T07:02:58.996Z vite:hmr [file change] src/components/HeavyPanel.vue [DEBUG HMR before-vue] 15:02:58 timestamp: 1790665378998 file: /src/components/HeavyPanel.vue modules: ["/src/components/HeavyPanel.vue","/src/components/HeavyPanel.vue?vue&type=style&index=0&scoped=c11907fb&lang.css"] [DEBUG HMR after-vue] 15:02:59 timestamp: 1790665378998 file: /src/components/HeavyPanel.vue modules: [] 2026-09-29T07:02:59.014Z vite:hmr (client) [no modules matched] src/components/HeavyPanel.vue 2026-09-29T07:02:59.014Z vite:hmr (ssr) [no modules matched] src/components/HeavyPanel.vue # read-evidence(+50ms): expected=499595 chars, onDisk=249797 chars, ctx.read()=499595 chars, fileHalfWritten=true, viteReadTruncated=false, legacyModules=[] # 2 no-payload latency=-ms payload=[null] ... # read-evidence(+4ms): expected=499595 chars, onDisk=249797 chars, ctx.read()=249797 chars, fileHalfWritten=true, viteReadTruncated=true, legacyModules=[] #15 no-payload latency=-ms payload=[null] # result: {"ok":1,"no-payload":14} # 14 of 15 saves lost their HMR update (ok=1) # evidence tally: 20 events sampled -> fileHalfWritten=true in 19;
